In this paper, our focus was on the case where the set of possible cluster centers M is the entire metric space. In the case where the metric is induced by a graph G = (V, E) (Section 5), it is also interesting to consider the case where M ⊂ V . Does a proportionally fair clustering always exist for trees when M ⊂ V , or for general graphs when N = M ⊂ V ? These questions remain open. More broadly, we find proportional fairness to be a very elegant fairness solution concept for clustering. Adapting this idea of proportional fairness to other machine learning settings such as regression or classification can lead to many avenues for future work.
